info.title: The Better Plate API
info.description: Versioned REST API for The Better Plate. Authentication uses session cookies issued by /v1/auth (email one-time code: POST /v1/auth/email-otp/send-verification-otp, then POST /v1/auth/sign-in/email-otp). Nutrition values are estimates computed from USDA FoodData Central records; not-reported nutrients are never zero.

nutrientsPer100g.description: Per 100 g as published. A missing key means not reported, never zero.

post.summary: Send an issue report (signed in or not)
post.description: Available on every screen, including sign-in and error states. The client shows the person exactly what is sent (message, readable recent steps, optional screenshot preview) before submitting. `id` makes retries from the offline queue idempotent.

get.summary: My planned and eaten meals for a date range (at most 31 days), or one of my profiles'
get.description: Plans and logs are returned separately and must never be added together. Each log carries its own immutable nutrition snapshot; `eaten` is per-serving nutrition × servings eaten. Writes go through POST /v1/sync/batch.

get.summary: My consumption goals
get.description: Goals the person set on what they eat. Writes go through POST /v1/sync/batch (goal.put, goal.delete).

get.summary: Estimated totals of what I ate over a range of days (at most 366)
get.description: Logged meals only; plans never count. Averages are per day with something logged, and `incomplete` says when some days have nothing logged. Nutrients no logged meal reports are unknown, never zero.

get.summary: What to buy for planned meals over a range of days (at most 31)
get.description: Mine by default; one of my profiles' with profileId; or a whole group's with groupId (owner or admin). Each food's grams are the recipe's amounts scaled to the servings planned; cooking oil counts what is added. Plans waiting for approval are counted apart, not listed. Only plans count; nothing eaten is involved.

get.summary: Food preferences in my kitchen: mine and my profiles'
get.description: Allergies, likes and dislikes as people stated them. The app always asks about allergies and records the answer; it never infers or diagnoses. Writes go through POST /v1/sync/batch (prefs.put).

get.summary: How my logged meals went (and my profiles')
get.description: Liked or not, a comment and ingredients not liked, one per eaten log. Writes go through POST /v1/sync/batch (feedback.put).

delete.description: Group recipes go back to the people who created them; meals the group planned stay in each person's kitchen as their own.

post.summary: Create a single-use invite link
post.description: The owner can invite admins or members; admins can invite members. Links work once and expire after 7 days. Anyone holding a link can use it, so share it privately.

get.summary: What an invite link is for (signed in)

post.summary: Join a group with an invite link
post.description: Members' own plans then wait for an admin's approval, and the group's admins can see and plan their meals.

put.summary: Make a person an admin or a member (owner)

422.description: Not a person, or the owner

delete.description: The owner can remove anyone else; anyone can remove themselves; a profile's owner can take it out. The owner cannot leave (end the group instead). Meals the group planned for a person who leaves stay in their kitchen as their own.

post.summary: Add a child's profile to a group (owner or admin)
post.description: Creates a profile owned by your account (no email, password or login, no birthdate) and adds it as a member. Its meals live in your kitchen.

put.summary: Record a profile's allergies, likes and dislikes (owner or admin)
put.description: For profiles (children) only: people record their own. Send If-Match with the version you edited, or nothing for a first answer. Allergies are what the family tells you; the app never infers them.

422.description: Not a profile, or unknown foods

get.summary: Every member's plans, eaten meals, feedback and preferences for a date range (owner or admin)
get.description: At most 31 days. Plans and eaten meals stay separate; a plan never counts as eaten.

post.summary: Plan a meal for a member (owner or admin)
post.description: The meal reaches the member's kitchen through sync; members can't change it. The answer carries an allergen alert from the member's listed allergies and the recipe's foods. It never blocks: the admin decides.

put.summary: Change a member's planned meal (owner or admin; If-Match)

Decline a meal a member planned for themselves

get.summary: The group's recipes (every member can read them)

post.summary: Copy one of my recipes into the group (owner or admin)
post.description: The copy is a group recipe: every admin can edit it, through sync or PUT /v1/recipes/{id}, and every member receives it. My original stays mine.

post.summary: Publish a read-only snapshot of the current saved version and get its link
post.description: Online only. The snapshot holds the title, description, servings, ingredients, the USDA-based estimate and, if chosen, the method and the photo. Anyone with the link can read it until it is revoked or expires.

get.summary: My active share links

delete.summary: Revoke a link; the snapshot is erased

get.summary: Read a shared recipe (no sign-in)
get.description: Returns only the approved snapshot fields. Revoked, expired and unknown links all answer 404.

get.summary: The photo of a shared recipe (no sign-in)
get.description: Only when the owner shared the photo. Stops working with the link: revoked, expired and unknown links all answer 404.

post.summary: Apply a batch of offline changes (protocol 1)
post.description: Operations apply in order, each in its own transaction, so a batch can partially succeed. Each opId is idempotent per user. A stale baseVersion returns status=conflict with the server copy; nothing is overwritten.

get.summary: Pull changes after a cursor, including deletion tombstones
get.description: Recipes (mine and my groups'), planned meals (including those my groups' admins planned for me), eaten logs, goals, food preferences, meal feedback and the profiles I own. When I join a group its recipes are sent again; when I leave one, clients drop its recipes.

get.summary: AI companion settings and today's usage

put.summary: Choose the provider, model and daily request limit
Connect a provider with your own API key
put.description: The key is checked with the provider, then stored encrypted. It is never returned, logged or sent to the browser again.

delete.summary: Disconnect a provider and erase its key

post.summary: One step of the companion: send a message or tool results, get text and tool calls
post.description: The app keeps the provider-native conversation and passes it back each step. Tool calls are validated against the tool schemas here; the app runs valid ones on the device and returns their results. Only per-day request and token counts are stored.

get.summary: Find openly licensed food photos from a description (Openverse)
get.description: q is a plain description ("grilled lemon chicken with rice"), matched against photo titles, descriptions and tags. If the full description finds too little, its main words are tried. Results are ordered by how many of the description's words they mention. Only public domain, CC0, CC BY and CC BY-SA photos are returned. Online only.

post.summary: Copy an Openverse photo into your kitchen
post.description: The server looks the photo up by its Openverse id (it never fetches a URL a client supplies), checks the license again, and downloads Openverse's resized copy. Credit and license are stored with it.

201.description: Stored; attach it to a recipe by id

post.summary: Generate a photorealistic recipe image
post.description: Uses the person's own OpenAI key when connected, otherwise the included companion (with its own daily image limit). The image is labelled AI-generated wherever it is shown and is not an exact depiction.

201.description: Stored; attach it to a recipe by id

post.summary: Upload your own photo
post.description: data is the file in base64 (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, GIF or TIFF, at most 9 MB). The person must confirm they took the photo or have the right to use it. The server re-encodes it to WebP (at most 1600 px) and drops all metadata, including location. Only its owner can see it.

201.description: Stored; attach it to a recipe by id
